name: Swapfeed
author: Mariofajt

sections.description:
Big platforms let people say “not interested”. Your site can too.

Swapfeed shows your posts as a clean card grid. Every card has a Not for me button. When a reader clicks it, the card disappears and another post slides into its place — the feed refills itself. After dismissing, the reader can also hide everything from that category with one click, or undo.

We call this pattern Dismiss & Refill: a self-curating feed that each reader shapes for themselves — the “not interested” / “show less like this” experience of Google Discover and YouTube, on your own WordPress site.

Use it for a personalized post feed, a blog index, a news grid, a portfolio, real estate listings or WooCommerce products.

Live demo: mariof.es/en/swapfeed. A working feed you can dismiss and refill.

Features

  • Shortcode [swapfeed] and a Swapfeed block for the block editor.
  • Works with any theme: inherits your fonts, uses your accent colour.
  • Posts, pages or any public custom post type; filter by category or tag.
  • Optional category filter buttons above the feed.
  • “Hide everything from this category”, Undo and Show hidden built in.
  • “Load more” button with infinite scroll after the first click.
  • Lightweight: one small script and stylesheet, loaded only where a feed is shown. No jQuery.
  • Private by design: what a reader hides is stored only in their own browser. No accounts, no tracking cookies.
  • What readers hide report: anonymous totals per category and the most dismissed posts, so you know what your audience doesn’t want (can be switched off).
  • Translation ready (translations are managed on translate.wordpress.org).
sections.installation:
1. Upload the swapfeed folder to /wp-content/plugins/ or install the zip from Plugins → Add New → Upload.
  2. Activate the plugin.
  3. Add the Swapfeed block to a page, or paste [swapfeed] anywhere shortcodes work.
  4. Adjust defaults in Settings → Swapfeed.
sections.faq:
Where are hidden posts stored?

In the reader’s browser (localStorage). They stay hidden on that device until the reader clicks “Show hidden” or clears site data.

Does it work with page caching?

Yes. The page is cached as usual; dismissing and refilling happen in the browser through the WordPress REST API.

Is the report GDPR friendly?

The report stores only anonymous daily totals per category and per post. No IP address, cookie or identifier is stored. A salted hash of the IP is kept for one hour only to limit abuse, then it expires.

Why are there public REST endpoints?

/wp-json/swapfeed/v1/items returns the same public post data that is already on the page (title, link, image, excerpt), so the feed can refill dismissed slots without reloading. /wp-json/swapfeed/v1/stat only accepts an action (dismiss / undo), a post ID and a term ID, validates that the post is published, and is limited to 120 events per hour per visitor. It can be switched off in Settings → Swapfeed.

Shortcode options?

count, columns, post_type, category, tag, exclude, offset, filters, image, excerpt, date, term, allow_term, title. Example: [swapfeed count="9" columns="3" category="news" filters="yes"]. Full list in Settings → Swapfeed → How to use.
sections.changelog:
1.0.3

  • Translations are now handled by translate.wordpress.org; bundled language files removed.

1.0.2

  • New filter swapfeed_taxonomy to choose the taxonomy used for labels, filter chips and “Hide everything from…” (e.g. a city taxonomy for real-estate listings).

1.0.1

  • New filter swapfeed_js_config so multilingual plugins can localise the REST URLs and labels.
  • Correct translation files (.mo) for every WordPress version.
  • Buttons ignore themes that force uppercase.

1.0.0

  • First release.
